title: Chevrolet Monte Carlo Engines (1970–2007)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevrolet Monte Carlo by year: the SS 454 of 1970–71, small blocks, the 1983–88 SS H.O. 305, V6s and the 2006–07 SS 5.3 V8.
intro: Chevrolet built the Monte Carlo as a rear-drive personal luxury coupe from 1970 to 1988 and as a front-drive coupe from 1995 to 2007. The SS name marked its performance versions: a 454 in 1970–1971, a high-output 305 in 1983–1988 and a 5.3 V8 in 2006–2007.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Monte Carlo shared the Chevelle's engines, from the 350 to the 402 big block badged as a 396, with the 454 in the SS. Ratings are gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972.
The Colonnade Monte Carlo offered the 350, 400 and 454, with the 454 available through 1975 and the 305 arriving for 1976.
The downsized Monte Carlo added V6s, including a turbocharged 3.8 in 1980–1981, and Oldsmobile-built diesels in the early 1980s. From 1983 the SS used a high-output 305.
The front-drive Monte Carlo used GM's 60-degree V6s and the 3800, supercharged in the 2004–2005 SS, and a 5.3 V8 in the 2006–2007 SS.
